questions.question: What type of algorithm is Merge Sort?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort is a classic example of a Divide and Conquer algorithm.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of Merge Sort in the worst case?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort has a time complexity of O(n log n) in all cases (worst, average, and best).

questions.question: Is Merge Sort a stable sorting algorithm?
questions.explanation: Stable sorting algorithms maintain the relative order of records with equal keys. Merge sort is a stable sort.

questions.question: Who invented the Merge Sort algorithm?
questions.explanation: John von Neumann invented the merge sort algorithm in 1945.

questions.question: What is the space complexity of Merge Sort?
questions.explanation: Merge sort requires a temporary array of size n to store the merged sub-arrays, so its space complexity is O(n).

questions.question: The 'merge' step in Merge Sort involves combining two...
questions.explanation: The core of the merge sort algorithm is the merging of two already sorted sub-arrays into a single sorted array.

questions.question: Merge Sort is a...?
questions.explanation: Since Merge Sort requires extra space proportional to the input size, it is not an in-place algorithm.

questions.question: The 'divide' step in Merge Sort recursively splits the array in...
questions.explanation: The 'divide' step of the algorithm involves recursively dividing the array into two halves until each sub-array contains a single element.

questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of Merge Sort?

options.text: It is not a stable sort
It has a worst-case time complexity of O(n^2)

questions.explanation: The main disadvantage of Merge Sort is that it requires O(n) auxiliary space.

questions.question: Merge sort is preferred for sorting...?
questions.explanation: Merge sort is often preferred for sorting linked lists because it doesn't require random access to elements and the merge operation can be implemented with O(1) space for linked lists.
